practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit secrets into code or logs; provide a .env.example with a placeholder only.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit secrets into code or logs; provide a .env.example with a placeholder only.

practices.practice: Create a single shared MongoClient (or AsyncMongoClient) at application startup and reuse it across the process rather than creating a client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single shared MongoClient/MotorClient at application startup and reuse it for all requests (do not create a new client per request); configure pool size to match FastAPI concurrency (maxPoolSize).

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) according to the runtime (serverless vs long-running) and expected concurrency rather than using arbitrary values.
Prefer PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient for async Python applications (rather than Motor) because Motor is deprecated for new async code; avoid mixing different driver types at runtime.
Use TLS for all connections and do not disable certificate verification in production; ensure tls=true and a valid CA bundle are available to the driver.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL for connections and avoid turning certificate validation off; prefer the connection string supplied by the service which includes tls options.

practices.practice: Create a TTL index on a Date field (e.g., retention_expires_at) with expireAfterSeconds (0 for absolute expiry) and remember TTL deletions are performed by a background job and can lag (not sub-minute precise).
practices.prior_belief: Enforce retention with a TTL index on a date field (e.g., expireAt or createdAt) and remember MongoDB TTL deletions are background/approximate (granularity and delay), so do not rely on sub-minute precision.

practices.practice: Model consent as append-only history embedded in the consent document for auditability, but if history can grow unbounded split it into a separate collection to avoid large-document problems.
practices.prior_belief: Model consent as append-only history inside the document for audit (push new entries to a history array and keep a derived current state fields like currentPreferences and consentVersion) but guard against unbounded array growth—if history may be large, store it in a separate collection.

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON limit: cap arrays, compress or spill large fields to child collections, and plan for steady-state growth, not just current size.
practices.prior_belief: Prevent document size explosion: consider capping history array length, compressing history entries, or moving history to a child collection when appending would risk hitting the BSON 16MB document limit.

practices.practice: Perform atomic single-document updates (e.g., findOneAndUpdate / updateOne with $push and $set or $each/$slice) to append history and update derived fields in one operation and avoid partial updates and race windows.
practices.prior_belief: Use atomic single-document updates (e.g., findOneAndUpdate with $push and $set) to append history and update derived current state in one operation, avoiding race conditions and minimizing the need for multi-document transactions.

practices.practice: Use optimistic concurrency (include a version or lastUpdated in update filters) when updates cannot safely be lost to concurrent requests.
practices.prior_belief: Implement optimistic concurrency control for updates that must not be lost (e.g., include a consentVersion or a lastUpdated timestamp in the filter of findOneAndUpdate) to avoid lost updates under concurrent requests.

practices.practice: Enable driver retry options (retryWrites=true, retryReads=true) and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for transient errors while ensuring write idempotency where needed.
practices.prior_belief: Enable driver-level retry options (retryWrites=true, retryReads=true) and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for transient network/timeout errors; be mindful of idempotency when retrying writes.

practices.practice: When you require the freshest read (e.g., current consent state), read from the primary; cross-region replicas are asynchronous and can return stale data.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer reading from the primary for the freshest consent state; set readPreference=primary (or design for eventual consistency if you can tolerate stale reads).

practices.practice: Multi-document transactions are supported but have limitations (e.g., supported within an unsharded collection and dependent on server-wire-protocol version); verify your cluster/server version before relying on cross-document transactions.
practices.prior_belief: If you need multi-document atomicity (e.g., update user profile plus consent across collections), use transactions but restrict their scope and payload size; verify MongoDB API/cluster version supports multi-document transactions in Azure DocumentDB.
practices.source_name: Microsoft Learn — Use Multi-document transactions in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB transactions support

practices.practice: Pin and verify compatible driver and ODM versions (PyMongo/AsyncMongoClient, Motor, Beanie) to the cluster's MongoDB wire protocol to avoid runtime incompatibilities and test on the target cluster version.
practices.prior_belief: Pin and verify compatible driver/ODM versions (Motor, PyMongo, Beanie) that match the cluster wire protocol (MongoDB server version) to avoid import/runtime incompatibilities; add the exact versions to requirements.txt.

practices.practice: When using an ODM (e.g., Beanie), use its model validation for input validation but also consider defense-in-depth because collection-level JSON schema support may vary; check service feature support for validator/$jsonSchema on your target server version.
practices.prior_belief: When using an ODM like Beanie, rely on its Pydantic models for input validation but also enforce server-side validation or schema validators at the collection level for defense in depth.
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB $jsonSchema feature search

practices.practice: Mask or redact connection strings and secrets in logs, exceptions, and telemetry; use structured logging with sensitive-field scrubbing.
practices.prior_belief: Mask or redact connection strings and secrets in logs, exceptions, and telemetry; use structured logging with sensitive field scrubbing.

practices.practice: Create and maintain indexes that support your API query patterns (equality → sort → range design, ESR ordering) and periodically inspect query plans with explain("executionStats") to detect and fix COLLSCANs.
practices.prior_belief: Create and maintain appropriate indexes for queries used by API endpoints (e.g., queries to fetch current preferences by customerId should be covered by an index) and periodically inspect query plans (explain) to detect COLLSCANs.

practices.practice: For vector search create a dedicated fixed-dimension vector field and a provider-specific vector index (choose DiskANN/HNSW/IVF by scale), normalize embeddings for cosine similarity, and tune index/query parameters (lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree).

Avoid mixing synchronous and asynchronous drivers in the runtime path (e.g., don't run pymongo sync client and Motor in the same event loop); if you must, keep them isolated (e.g., synchronous seeding scripts separate from async app runtime).
practices.prior_belief: Avoid mixing synchronous pymongo and asynchronous Motor clients in the same process for runtime usage; if you must use both (e.g., for seeding), keep them separated and prefer one for the app runtime to avoid compatibility and event-loop issues.

practices.practice: Provision the cluster size / compute tier and throughput appropriate to expected write/read workload patterns (use autoscale where helpful) and monitor for 429 throttling to trigger scaling/back-off.
practices.prior_belief: Provision appropriate throughput (RU/s or instance sizing) for expected write-heavy workloads (e.g., consent updates) and consider autoscale or appropriate tier to avoid throttling; monitor for 429/Throttling errors and back off.

practices.practice: Include actor, timestamp and reason metadata in each appended history entry so consent changes form a clear, auditable, immutable trail.
practices.prior_belief: Log and audit consent changes (actor id, timestamp, ip, reason) in each appended history entry to provide a clear, queryable audit trail; treat audit entries as immutable records.

practices.practice: On Azure DocumentDB prefer the native 'textSearch' + $search capabilities instead of community $text indexes when building full-text search experiences.
